stories.title: Japan police to expand wearable camera use nationwide in FY2027
stories.summary: The Japanese police will expand use of body-worn cameras nationwide from fiscal 2027 after trials showed they were effective in providing evidence and verifying that investigative procedures were followed appropriately, the National. Police Agency said on Aug 28. The agency has requested about 170 million yen (S$1.4 million) for the year starting April 2027 to cover related costs for around 2,000 cameras. Trials began in September 2025 in 13 prefectural police departments, covering community affairs, traffic enforcement and crowd control operations. Trials were conducted for community affairs in Tokyo, Osaka and Fukuoka prefectures until November. Footage was used as evidence in a case of obstruction of official duties, in which a Fukuoka Prefectural. Police officer who had intervened to mediate a dispute – while the incident, including police questioning, was being recorded – was kicked by a man. In another case, a suspect in drug-related cases claimed to have been forcibly taken in for questioning, but video footage confirmed that there were no issues. While Niigata, Aichi and Kochi prefectural polices conducted trials in traffic enforcement operations for six months, supervisors used footage on around 160 occasions to check whether procedures for catching traffic offenders had been done by the book. Some drivers who were stopped by the police said they think it is good that cameras record questioning, according to the agency. Year-long trials for crowd control in public places, such as event venues and railway stations, are being conducted by the police in nine prefectures, including Hokkaido and Hiroshima. In more than 10 cases during the three kinds of trials, people showed resistance to being filmed.

stories.title: Global foundry market grows 29 pct in Q2 on strong AI chip demand: report
stories.summary: SEOUL, Aug. 28 (Yonhap) -- The global pure-play semiconductor foundry market gre...
article_sentences: The global pure-play semiconductor foundry market grew 29 percent on-year in the second quarter, driven by a massive boom in artificial intelligence (AI) chip demand, an industry report showed Friday.
Counterpoint Research said AI-related orders and capacity reallocation remain key drivers of supply-demand imbalances in both advanced and mature nodes.
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.
(TSMC) remained the market leader with a 73 percent share in the cited period, taking the top spot for two consecutive quarters.

Counterpoint Research attributed TSMC's strong performance largely to the mass production of chips using its 2-nanometer process, the expansion of 3-nanometer production, and supply shortages in mature 8-inch and 12-inch processes as well as advanced packaging.
Samsung Electronics Co.
maintained the No.
2 spot, with its market share remaining relatively unchanged from the previous quarter.
Samsung Foundry's major target is still on improving SF2's yield rate.
However, demand from SF4 and SF5 is also a key driver of revenue growth in addition to the foundry wafer price increase in the first half of the year.
